terms: fg(x) means apply g first, then f: fg(x) = f(g(x)). Order matters; fg(x) ≠ gf(x) in general.
Domain is the set of valid inputs; range is the set of outputs produced. For f(x)=√x, domain x≥0, range f(x)≥0.
A mapping f: X → Y assigning exactly one y to each x in the domain X. Written y = f(x).
f⁻¹ reverses f: f(f⁻¹(x)) = x. Exists only if f is one-to-one. Domain of f⁻¹ = range of f.
|x| = x if x≥0, else −x. Graph is V-shaped, vertex at origin. |f(x)|=k gives two equations: f(x)=±k.
y = f(x)+a translates up by a; y = f(x+a) translates left by a; y = af(x) stretches vertically; y = f(ax) compresses horizontally.
Angles on a line, around a point, in triangles and parallel lines.
Interior and exterior angles of polygons.
Angle and chord properties of circles.
Identical shapes versus same shape, different size.
Accurate drawings using compasses and a ruler.

Bar charts, pie charts and histograms.
Choosing a representative sample of a population.
Rate of change of f at x: f'(x) = limₕ→₀ [f(x+h) − f(x)]/h. Geometric meaning: gradient of tangent.
d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹ for any real n. Linear: d/dx(c f(x)) = c f'(x).
If y = f(x), then dy/dt = (dy/dx)(dx/dt). Used in related-rates problems (e.g., expanding circles, draining tanks).
f''(x) = d²y/dx². f''(x) > 0 indicates concave up (minimum); f''(x) < 0 indicates concave down (maximum).
d/dx(sin x) = cos x; d/dx(cos x) = −sin x; d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ; d/dx(ln x) = 1/x.
Points where f'(x) = 0. Use second derivative or sign change to classify max, min, or point of inflection.
logₐ x = logᵦ x / logᵦ a. Useful when calculator only has log₁₀ or ln.
y = aˣ with a > 0, a ≠ 1. Grows rapidly if a > 1; decays if 0 < a < 1. Always passes through (0, 1).
log(xy) = log x + log y; log(x/y) = log x − log y; log(xⁿ) = n log x. Same base throughout.
logₐ x is the inverse of aˣ: logₐ x = y ⟺ aʸ = x. Natural log: ln x = logₑ x.
Population growth, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling: all use y = Aeᵏᵗ. Log transforms linearise data.
y = eˣ where e ≈ 2.71828. Unique property: d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ. Used for continuous growth/decay.
F ≤ μR (where R = normal reaction, μ = coefficient of friction). Limiting friction reached when motion impending.
A body remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless acted on by a resultant force.
F = ma. Resultant force on a body equals mass times acceleration. Vector equation.
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Forces come in pairs on different bodies.
Split forces into perpendicular components (e.g., horizontal/vertical or along/perpendicular to inclined plane).
Mass m is amount of matter (kg). Weight W = mg (newtons). On Earth, g ≈ 9.8 N/kg.
If f(x) ≥ 0 on [a, b], the definite integral gives the area. Negative regions subtract.
∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a). Represents net signed area between curve and x-axis from a to b.
∫f(x) dx = F(x) + C where F'(x) = f(x). C is the constant of integration.
∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C for n ≠ −1. For n = −1: ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C.
∫sin x dx = −cos x + C; ∫cos x dx = sin x + C; ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C; ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C.
V = π ∫ₐᵇ y² dx (rotation about x-axis). V = π ∫ y² dy or π ∫ₓ² dy (about y-axis).

Point where weight of a body acts. For uniform rod, lies at midpoint. For composite shapes, use moments to find it.
Body in equilibrium if resultant force = 0 AND resultant moment about any point = 0.
Turning effect of a force about a point: moment = force × perpendicular distance from pivot. Units: Nm.
For equilibrium, sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments about same point.
Beams on supports: each support provides a normal reaction. Use moments and force balance to find magnitudes.
Beam about to tip when reaction at one support becomes zero. Useful for limit-case problems.
If f is continuous and f(a) · f(b) < 0, there is a root in (a, b). Useful to locate roots before refining.
Newton-Raphson typically converges quadratically; fixed-point iteration linearly. Some methods diverge.
Overestimates if curve is concave down; underestimates if concave up. Error decreases as n increases.
Rearrange equation as x = g(x). Iterate xₙ₊₁ = g(xₙ) from start value. Converges if |g'(x)| < 1 near root.
xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f'(xₙ). Fast convergence to root if starting value near root and f'(x) ≠ 0.
Approximates ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx ≈ (h/2)[y₀ + 2(y₁ + ... + yₙ₋₁) + yₙ] with strip width h = (b − a)/n.
P(A|B) = P(B|A) · P(A) / P(B). Updates beliefs given new evidence. Used in medical testing, spam filtering.
P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B). Probability of A given B has occurred.
Events A, B independent ⟺ P(A ∩ B) = P(A) · P(B). Equivalently, P(A|B) = P(A).
0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1; P(Ω) = 1; mutually exclusive events: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).
Branches show sequential outcomes with conditional probabilities. Multiply along branches; add at endpoints.
Visualise sets and intersections. Useful for P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
Many proofs (identities, inequalities) reduce to careful algebra: factorisation, completing the square, AM-GM.
Assume the hypotheses; deduce the conclusion by valid steps. Most common form for identities and divisibility.
If P then Q is not the same as if Q then P. Be careful with converses; quantifiers (∀, ∃) change meaning.
Assume the negation; derive a contradiction; conclude original statement. Classic: irrationality of √2.
Disprove a universal claim by exhibiting a single case where it fails. One counterexample suffices.
Base case + inductive step (assume true for n = k, prove for n = k + 1). Used for sums, divisibility, inequalities.

Sequence converges if it tends to a finite limit; diverges otherwise. Series converges if partial sums approach a finite limit.
Constant ratio r between terms. nth term: uₙ = ar^(n−1). Sum: Sₙ = a(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r) for r ≠ 1.
Defines each term using earlier terms: uₙ₊₁ = f(uₙ). E.g., uₙ₊₁ = 2uₙ + 1, u₁ = 3.
Σ symbol denotes summation: Σₖ₌₁ⁿ aₖ means a₁ + a₂ + ... + aₙ.

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for all θ. Derived from the unit circle. Source of related identities.

Vector of length 1 in direction of a: â = a/|a|. Used to specify direction without magnitude.
Quantity with magnitude and direction. Written as column or i-j form: a = (3, 4) or 3i + 4j.
